note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is not pictured, Job is not portrayed as a biblical person but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: No mortal can win a case against God: if a man tried to argue with him, he could not answer him once in a thousand times.
ideas: A lone man stands at a small table in a vast empty courtroom, looking up at a judge's bench that towers like a cliff into bright light
A man presses his palms against a sheer granite cliff that rises out of sight, as if to push it back
A schoolboy stands at a blackboard covered from edge to edge with questions he cannot answer
A man in a rowboat strains at the oars against the foot of a huge waterfall
A single candle stands in the full glare of the noon sun
A man holds one thin sheet of paper before a wall of a thousand filing drawers
A small boat in front of a towering sea cliff
A man stands at a witness box, mouth open, with no words coming
A man leans his shoulder against a vast concrete dam
A child squares up to the ocean surf with his fists raised

sections.meaning: God's power is beyond measure: he moves mountains, shakes the earth, commands the sun, spreads out the heavens, walks on the sea and made the stars.
ideas: A whole mountain breaks apart and slides, its peak tilting and dust pouring down, the ground below split open
A row of mountain peaks lies overturned on their sides like toppled stones
The ground of a valley split by a long fresh crack, the far mountains shrouded in falling rock
A town at what should be morning, the sky still black and the street lights still on
A man stands small on a night seashore under a sky blazing with countless stars as great waves break
Huge waves under an immense starry sky with the Milky Way arching overhead, no land in sight
Storm clouds stretched across the whole sky like a tent being pitched over the earth
A lighthouse dwarfed by a towering wave
A telescope on a hill pointed at the Milky Way
A child's hand pointing up at the Pleiades on a clear night

sections.meaning: God passes by unseen and takes away as he wills, and no one can stop him or ask him what he is doing.
ideas: A great gust sweeps across a wheat field past a man, flattening the wheat round him; he turns but sees nothing
A sudden gust tears a man's hat and papers from his hands and whirls them away into an empty sky
Curtains billow into a room through an open window while a man turns to look and sees no one
Leaves whirl past a man on an empty street in a wind he cannot see
Footprints appear in fresh snow beside a man with no one making them
A man reaches for a kite as the wind tears its string from his hand
A tide pulls a man's belongings out to sea while he stands helpless on the shore
A door slams in the wind in an empty house
Ripples cross a still lake from nothing that can be seen
A man shouts after a speeding train that has already gone

sections.meaning: Even if Job is in the right he cannot make his case: he can only plead, he doubts he is heard, and he is battered without cause and given no time to breathe.
ideas: A man on a hilltop at night calls out with his hands cupped round his mouth into a vast silent dark
A man kneels alone in an enormous dim hall with clasped hands, pleading toward a high window of light
A man sits up late with a phone pressed to his ear, eyes closed, unsure anyone is there
A man struggles bent double along a road in a violent storm, rain lashing him, gasping for breath
A man waist-deep in a rough sea as wave after wave breaks over him with no time to breathe
A man drops his prepared notes on the floor of a courtroom, speechless
A boxer's corner with no one in it
A man pressed against a door in a gale, trying to get inside
Hail beats down on a man without shelter
A man with his own hand clapped over his mouth

sections.meaning: Job sees no justice on earth: the blameless and the wicked are destroyed alike, the world is in the hands of the wicked, and its judges are blinded.
ideas: A flood has sunk two neighbouring houses alike, one neat with flower boxes, one neglected and boarded up
A hailstorm has flattened a tended garden and a neighbour's weedy junk yard alike
Three judges at the bench hold their hands over their eyes while a smug man in an expensive suit walks free
A smug man in a skyscraper office turns a globe of the earth in his hand like a toy
Two identical blank headstones side by side in a quiet field
Lady Justice's scales lying broken on the floor
A wildfire burns through an orchard and a thorn patch alike
A rich man's limousine splashes mud over a waiting poor family
A gavel lies unused under dust on an empty bench
A judge's chair with a dark cloth thrown over it

sections.meaning: His days rush by without seeing any good; he cannot smile his pain away, and however clean he makes himself he would still be plunged into filth.
ideas: A sprinter streaks past at full speed on an empty road, a blur of motion
An eagle in a steep dive at full speed over a lake
Light boats shoot past on a fast river current
A tired man at a mirror tries to force a cheerful smile, but his eyes are full of pain
A man holds a bright smiling mask in front of his drawn, sad face
A man in a spotless white shirt stands chest-deep in a pit of black mud, still holding a bar of soap
A man kneels in clean snow scrubbing his raw hands, a pit of black mud open beside him
Freshly washed white laundry on a line splashed with mud by a passing truck
A man shovels sand uphill as it slides back down
Seasons flash past a window in one frame, spring to winter

sections.meaning: God is not a man Job can meet in court, and there is no one between them to bring them together; he longs to speak without fear.
ideas: A man sits alone on one side of a long table; the far side is flooded with blinding light; the go-between's chair at the head stands empty
A man at the edge of a canyon where the bridge across has fallen away, the far side in light
Two hands reach toward each other across a gap no one bridges
An empty referee's chair at the net of an empty court
A man waits alone outside an enormous closed door with no one to go in with him
A phone with no line between two houses
A man trembling at a podium in a vast dark hall, unable to speak
A man standing in the long cold shadow of a storm cloud
A child stands between two parents holding both their hands, beside an empty space where that child is missing
A rope bridge with its middle planks gone

scenes.principle: How can a mortal be in the right with God? No one who sets himself against him comes out whole.
scenes.shows: A lone man leans his whole weight against a sheer granite cliff that rises out of sight into the clouds, as if to push it back.
scenes.prompt: A lone man in plain everyday clothes stands at the foot of an immense sheer granite cliff that rises straight up out of sight into the clouds. He has both palms pressed flat against the rock, leaning his whole weight into it as if to push it back, and he is tiny against it. Overcast daylight.

scenes.principle: He moves mountains and overturns them, and shakes the earth from its place.
scenes.shows: A row of great mountain peaks lies overturned on their sides like toppled stones, dust still rising where they stood.
scenes.prompt: A vast mountain range seen from far off under a clear blue sky. A whole row of its great rocky peaks has been overturned and lies tipped over on their sides like toppled stones, their roots in the air, with dust still rising from the earth where they stood. No buildings, no roads.

scenes.principle: He alone stretches out the heavens, treads on the sea and made the stars: wonders beyond number.
scenes.shows: A man stands small on a night seashore under a sky blazing with countless stars, the Milky Way arching overhead, as great waves break.
scenes.prompt: On a rocky seashore at night a man in an ordinary jacket stands very small at the water's edge, looking up at an immense sky blazing with countless stars, the Milky Way arching overhead from one horizon to the other, the bright constellations standing out clearly. In front of him huge waves rise and break white in the starlight.

scenes.principle: He passes by unseen and snatches away, and no one can turn him back.
scenes.shows: On a windy hilltop a sudden gust tears a man's hat and papers from his hands and whirls them away into an empty sky.
scenes.prompt: On an open grassy hilltop on a bright, windy day, a man turns as a sudden gust tears his hat and a sheaf of papers out of his hands and whirls them high up and away into an empty blue sky. He reaches after them with one arm, but they are already far beyond him. The grass all round is flattened by the wind.

scenes.principle: Even in the right, Job could only plead, and would not believe he was being heard.
scenes.shows: At night on a hilltop a man calls out with his hands cupped round his mouth into the vast silent dark.
scenes.prompt: At night on a bare hilltop above a wide dark valley, a man stands with his hands cupped round his mouth, calling out with all his strength into the vast silent darkness. Nothing answers. A few far stars, a thin moon, and the faint lights of a sleeping town far below.

scenes.principle: He strikes me with a storm and does not let me get my breath back.
scenes.shows: A man struggles along a road in a violent storm, bent into the wind and rain, gasping for breath.
scenes.prompt: A man struggles along an open country road in a violent storm, bent almost double into the wind, rain lashing him sideways, his clothes soaked through, one arm raised against the blast, his mouth open gasping for breath. Dark churning clouds fill the sky, and the fields on both sides are streaming with water.

scenes.principle: It is all one: he makes an end of the blameless and the wicked alike.
scenes.shows: A flood has sunk two neighbouring houses alike, one neat with flower boxes, the other neglected and boarded up.
scenes.prompt: Seen from a little above, a flood of brown water has risen over a street, and two houses side by side are both sunk up to their windows. One is neat and freshly painted, with a tended garden and flowers in its window boxes; the other is neglected, its windows boarded up and its yard full of junk. The flood has taken both alike. Grey sky.

scenes.principle: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked, and the faces of its judges are covered.
scenes.shows: Three judges at the bench sit with their hands over their eyes while a smug man in an expensive suit walks free.
scenes.prompt: In a present-day courtroom, three judges in plain black judicial gowns sit at the high bench, and each of them holds a hand pressed over their eyes. In front of the bench a smug, well-fed man in an expensive suit strolls away free, smiling, a leather briefcase in his hand.

scenes.principle: My days are swifter than a runner; they flee and see no good.
scenes.shows: A sprinter streaks past on an empty country road, a blur of speed.
scenes.prompt: On an empty road through open country at midday, a sprinter races past at full speed, caught as a streaking blur of motion from left to right, his feet barely touching the road. Everything else, the road, the fields and the sky, is sharp and still.

scenes.principle: If I say I will put off my sad face and be cheerful, I still dread all my pains.
scenes.shows: A tired man at a bathroom mirror forces a smile, but his eyes are red and full of pain.
scenes.prompt: A tired middle-aged man stands at a bathroom mirror in the morning, trying to force a cheerful smile at his reflection. In the mirror his mouth is smiling, but his eyes are red and full of pain, and the smile does not reach them. Soft window light.

scenes.principle: Though I washed myself with snow, you would plunge me into the pit.
scenes.shows: A man in a clean white shirt stands chest-deep in a pit of black mud in the snow, still holding a bar of soap.
scenes.prompt: A man in a spotless, freshly washed white shirt stands chest-deep in a deep pit of thick black mud, still holding a bar of white soap in one hand, looking down at the mud already smeared over his clean shirt. Clean white snow lies on the ground all round the rim of the pit. Bright winter daylight.

scenes.principle: He is not a man like me, and there is no one between us to lay his hand on us both.
scenes.shows: A man stands at the edge of a canyon where the bridge across has fallen away, its broken ends hanging on both sides.
scenes.prompt: A man in plain clothes stands at the edge of a deep rocky canyon where a bridge once crossed: only its broken ends remain, hanging from both cliffs, with nothing between them. The far side of the canyon is bathed in bright light. Clear daylight.
